transcript.content: Hello. What brings you into the clinic today?

Well, honestly, I'm only sitting here because my husband basically forced me to come. He and, well, all the people down at the warehouse where I work, they keep acting like I'm crazy or something. Like I'm just making things up out of thin air. But I'm not. I've been moving freight there for a long time, and I know exactly what's going on. 

See, they have been watching my every move. I can feel them staring when I'm out on the floor. And it's not just looking—they are actively messing with my work. I'll load up a pallet, right? Get it all wrapped, count the boxes, log it in. I know my numbers, I'm good at my job. But then I'll walk away for two seconds to grab the pallet jack, and when I check the system later, the pallet counts are changed. They are deliberately going into the system and changing my numbers behind my back! 

And I know exactly why they're doing it, too. There’s a supervisor spot opening up, and I’ve been working my tail off for it, so they’re doing all this... this sabotage. Changing my counts and watching me from the racks, just to make me look bad so they can keep me from getting that supervisor spot. And instead of backing me up, my husband just takes their side and says I need to see a doctor. So, that's why I'm here. Even though I'm the only one actually paying attention to what they're doing to me.
That sounds like a very stressful experience to go through. How long have you been noticing these things happening at work?

Well, it’s been a while now. I’d say, if I really think back on it, it’s been about eight months. Yeah, eight months of this constant... this constant feeling of being watched, and the numbers being messed with. And, you know, it’s not just the staring and the pallets, either. There are the voices, too. I started hearing them right around the same time, about eight months ago. 

At first, I thought it was just the warehouse noise, you know? It’s loud in there—forklifts beeping, the big bay doors rattling, people shouting across the floor. But then I realized the voices weren't coming from the floor. They were, like, right there, talking about me. Whispering about how I was messing up, or how I wasn't going to get the promotion. And it’s just been going on and on for eight whole months. Every single shift, I go in there, and I have to deal with the eyes on me, the system getting hacked to change my counts, and those voices just chiming in. 

And my husband, he thinks I'm just stressed because of the supervisor spot, but how can I not be stressed when this has been my life for eight months? I mean, anybody would be on edge if they had to deal with that kind of sabotage day in and day out for that long. It’s exhausting, it really is. I just want to do my job and get what I earned, but they’ve been at this for eight months straight, just trying to break me down.
During these past eight months, have you had periods where you felt persistently down, sad, or depressed most of the day?

No, no, I haven't been sad. I mean, sure, I get frustrated, obviously. Like I said, who wouldn't be frustrated when people are constantly messing with your work and changing your numbers? It makes you want to pull your hair out! But sad? Depressed? No, definitely not. I haven't been sitting around crying or moping or anything like that. 

If anything, I've just been angry. And determined. I am so determined to prove that I am doing my job right, you know? I go into that warehouse every day, and I keep my head up, and I do my work, even with all the whispering and the staring. I don't let them see me down. I don't have time to be depressed. I have to stay sharp, because if I don't pay attention for even a second, that's when they sneak into the system. So, no, I'm not depressed. I'm just tired of the sabotage. My husband keeps trying to say I'm acting depressed, but he just doesn't get it. He doesn't see what I have to deal with every single day on that floor. He just sits in his office all day, he has no idea what it's like to have people actively trying to ruin your life for eight months straight. So, no, definitely not sad. Just... fed up. Extremely fed up with the whole situation.
Have you been diagnosed with any physical health conditions or medical problems?

Physical health conditions? No, no, I don't have anything like that. I mean, my body is fine. I work in a warehouse, you know? I'm moving freight all day long. You can't do that kind of work if you've got medical problems. I'm lifting heavy boxes, pulling pallets, walking miles and miles on that concrete floor every single shift. My back gets a little sore sometimes, sure, but that's just from the job, not some kind of disease or condition. 

I actually think I'm in better shape than most of the people there. Especially the ones who spend all their time huddled up behind the racks, whispering and trying to figure out how to mess with my counts. If they actually did some real work instead of just standing around plotting against me, maybe they'd be as strong as I am. But no, no doctor has ever told me I have any physical problems. I don't take any pills for my heart or my blood pressure or anything like that. My husband, he’s got the high cholesterol, but me? I’m perfectly healthy. Physically, anyway. It’s just... it’s just the stress of having to watch my back every single minute I'm on the clock. That’s the only thing wearing me down. But no, no medical conditions at all. I'm solid as a rock when it comes to that.
Do you drink alcohol or use any recreational drugs or substances?

No, no, I don't touch any of that stuff. I mean, I don't even drink, not even a beer after work. Some of the guys on the floor, they go out to the bar down the street, you know, the one with the neon sign that's always flickering? They go there after second shift and just get completely wasted. But I never go with them. How could I? If I go out and get drunk, or, I don't know, smoke something, my mind would be foggy. And I can't afford a foggy mind, not with what's going on. 

I have to be sharp. Like I said, they're always watching, always waiting for me to slip up so they can mess with the system and change my numbers. If I was hungover, or high, or whatever, I wouldn't be able to catch them. I wouldn't hear the whispers as clearly, or notice when the pallets are moved just that little bit to throw me off. I need all my senses working at a hundred percent. 

My husband sometimes has a glass of whiskey on the weekends, and he'll ask if I want one to "unwind." Unwind! Can you believe that? How am I supposed to unwind when I know the minute I go back to work on Monday, the sabotage starts all over again? Alcohol just makes you sloppy, and I refuse to be sloppy. I don't take any drugs, either. No pills, no weed, nothing. I just drink coffee—lots of coffee, actually, from the breakroom machine, even though it tastes like burnt dirt—just to stay alert. So, no, absolutely no drugs or alcohol. I need to keep my head completely clear to deal with this whole mess.
